text:
Alex Chen: Heads up — after the merges this morning I'm seeing CI perf fail on long-prefix decode workloads: p95 decode latency up ~30% on `seq=4096` runs. Repro locally with the perf harness. link: https://perf.internal/runs/17999 :frowning:
Priya Rao: Ugh. Which merges are you blaming? any recent fused-op or kernel selector changes? :eyes:
Dan M.: There were two related PRs that landed near each other: #2479 (kernel-selection heuristics refactor) and #2481 (small reshape/fused-op micro-optim). Both merged before the CI run. ci-bot posted the perf regression alert at 1799901180.
Sara L.: I ran a quick local with the same model and seq length: `./perf/run --model gpt-3-small --seq 4096 --iter 5` and see the same spike in token time after token ~128 (warm cache). flamegraph snapshot: `attention_kernel_dispatch` width balloons.
Dan M.: I started a `git bisect` between commit c3b9f (pre-merge baseline) and f2a7d (post-merge head). Early bisect points at 9f3a2c which contains the kernel selection threshold changes in `kernel_selector.cpp`.
Priya Rao: Can you paste the minimal failing command you used to bisect? I can try to reproduce on my workstation.
Dan M.: repro commands: ```bash
git checkout 9f3a2c
make -j8 && ./build/infer_perf --model gpt-small --seq 4096 --batch 1 --tokens 1024
```
Alex Chen: Interesting — 9f3a2c adjusts `prefer_fused_attention` to true for small batch sizes and tweaks the heuristic that picks the CUDA kernel for >128 prefix. That could route requests to the slower fallback for long prefixes.
Priya Rao: I pulled 9f3a2c and instrumented `kernel_selector` with timing logs: `selected_kernel=attn_v2, score=0.72, fallback=true`. The fallback flag seems wrong: score should have picked `attn_v3_fast`.
Dan M.: Looked at assembly; attn_v3_fast requires a small pre-copy of KV buffers that used to be elided. The reshape micro-op PR added a memmove path that forces a copy for cached KV in some code paths. Combined with the selector change that de-prioritizes attn_v3 unless copy cost < threshold, we hit the slow path. Two small changes interacting.
Alex Chen: OK plan: revert the selector heuristic commit 9f3a2c into staging and run the full perf harness canary. If that fixes, we do a rollback PR and then rework both patches for correctness. Anyone object? :+1:
Sara L.: Sounds right. I can spin up the staging canary cluster and run the `long-prefix` suite. ETA ~30m.
ci-bot: Perf CI: Regression detected in job `inference-long-prefix` — p95 +31% vs baseline. Link: https://ci.internal/job/2345
Alex Chen: Staging revert results: after cherry-picking the revert, p95 dropped back to +2% (within noise). Repro run attached: https://perf.internal/runs/18002 — looks like selector revert fixes most of the regression.
Dan M.: Good catch. I'll open a rollback PR for 9f3a2c with notes and start a follow-up that updates the fused-op memmove to avoid eager copies for KV cache.
Priya Rao: Please add a test in the perf harness that exercises `seq=4096` with cached KV paths so this doesn't sneak back in.
Alex Chen: Agreed. I'll add a CI perf guard for long-prefix loads and mark the rollout blocker flag on the original micro-op PR until we rework it. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Sara L.: Filed canary task and schedule for controlled canary rollout at 11:30 PT.
Dan M.: Opening rollback PR now: https://git.internal/r/rollbacks/456 — tagging @product if they want a note.
Alex Chen: Closing loop: once rollback merges I'll reassign follow-ups to Dan/Priya for the two fix PRs and add perf tests. Great quick triage.
